title: Forced Collectivization of Agriculture Launched

reason: Kremikovtsi was part of the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1961-1965), not the First. Decision to build Kremikovtsi made 1956; construction started 1960; opened 1963. Attributing it to the First Five-Year Plan is materially wrong.

title: Death of Stalin Triggers Limited De-Stalinization in Bulgaria
reason: Stalin died March 1953; Chervenkov began loosening Stalinist controls under Soviet pressure; partial prisoner releases confirmed.

title: Todor Zhivkov Elected BCP First Secretary
reason: March 1954, Zhivkov elected First Secretary of Central Committee, youngest bloc leader at the time. Confirmed by Wikipedia and Britannica.

title: Bulgaria Admitted to the United Nations
reason: December 14, 1955, as part of 16-member package deal via Security Council Resolution 109. All details confirmed.

title: Bulgaria Joins the Warsaw Pact
reason: Bulgaria was a founding signatory on May 14, 1955. Confirmed.

title: Khrushchev's Secret Speech Accelerates Bulgarian De-Stalinization
reason: Chervenkov lost PM post; Anton Yugov replaced him; Zhivkov criticized Chervenkov at April 1956 plenum. All confirmed.

title: Zhivkov Combines Party and State Leadership
reason: November 19, 1962, Zhivkov elected PM. He held both First Secretary and PM roles until 1971 (then shifted to State Council Chairman). Confirmed.

title: Kremikovtsi Steel Plant Opens as Communist Showcase
reason: Year is wrong. Kremikovtsi Iron and Steel Works opened November 5, 1963, not 1962. Construction began 1960. Year-off by 1 = FALSE.

title: April Plot Military Coup Attempt Against Zhivkov Foiled
reason: April 1965 coup attempt by military officers and party members confirmed. Foiled April 8-12, 1965; conspirators imprisoned.

title: Bulgaria Participates in Warsaw Pact Invasion of Czechoslovakia
reason: Bulgaria was one of four Warsaw Pact nations that invaded August 20-21, 1968. Brezhnev Doctrine endorsement confirmed.

title: New Socialist Constitution Makes Zhivkov Head of State
reason: 1971 Zhivkov Constitution created State Council Chairman post; Zhivkov assumed it, combining with First Secretary role. Confirmed.

title: Kozloduy Nuclear Plant Unit 1 Enters Commercial Operation
reason: Unit 1 physically started June 30, 1974; connected to grid July 24, 1974; formally opened September 4, 1974. Confirmed.

title: Bulgaria Signs Helsinki Final Act
reason: Bulgaria signed the Helsinki Final Act at the CSCE Conference in 1975. Confirmed.

title: Pravets Personal Computer Production Begins
reason: Year is wrong. Pravets computer development began 1979; IMKO-1 prototype shown publicly 1981; mass production (Pravetz 82) started 1982. No production in 1975.

title: Georgi Markov Assassinated with Ricin Umbrella in London
reason: September 7, 1978; ricin pellet injected into his leg via modified umbrella at London bus stop; died September 11. All confirmed.

title: Bulgaria Celebrates 1300th Anniversary of Statehood
reason: 1300-year celebrations of First Bulgarian Empire (681 AD) in 1981, orchestrated by Lyudmila Zhivkova. Confirmed.

title: Revival Process â€” Forced Renaming of 800,000 Ethnic Turks
reason: Campaign started June 1984; over 800,000 forced name changes confirmed (estimates 720,000-820,000 Turks + Roma). Turkish language banned, arrests confirmed.

title: Chernobyl Fallout Reaches Bulgaria â€” Authorities Downplay Risk
reason: April 1986 Chernobyl fallout reached Bulgaria; regime downplayed risk; suppressed independent assessment. Confirmed.

title: Ruse Environmental Protest â€” First Major Public Dissent

title: Expulsion of 360,000 Ethnic Turks â€” Largest Postwar Forced Migration in Europe
reason: May-August 1989, approximately 360,000 expelled. Described as Cold War Europe's largest ethnic cleansing. Turkey closed borders due to influx. All confirmed.

title: Ecoglasnost Protest at CSCE Conference Embarrasses Regime
reason: October 1989 Sofia CSCE follow-up meeting; Ecoglasnost petition broadcast internationally. Confirmed.

title: Zhivkov Removed from Power After 35-Year Rule
reason: November 10, 1989 (day after Berlin Wall fell); internal Politburo coup; Petar Mladenov led ouster. 35-year rule confirmed.

title: Roundtable Talks Produce Agreement on Free Elections
reason: Roundtable negotiations between BCP/BSP and UDF; agreements on free elections and constitutional reform confirmed.

title: Bulgaria Defaults on $11 Billion Foreign Debt

reason: June 1990 elections; BSP (renamed BCP) won parliamentary majority over UDF. Confirmed.

title: New Democratic Constitution Adopted
reason: Adopted July 12, 1991 by 7th Grand National Assembly; parliamentary republic established. Confirmed.

reason: October 1991 elections; UDF narrowly won; Filip Dimitrov formed first non-communist government since 1944. Confirmed.

title: Zhivkov Convicted of Embezzlement and Placed Under House Arrest
reason: Zhivkov convicted of embezzlement and abuse of power; sentenced to house arrest. Confirmed.

title: Bulgarian Socialist Party Returns to Power â€” Statist Economic Reversal
reason: BSP won 1994 elections; Zhan Videnov government reversed privatization; set up 1996-97 crisis. Confirmed.

title: Banking Collapse and Hyperinflation Devastate Economy
reason: Banking system collapse 1996; lev lost ~90% value; hyperinflation peaked at 242% monthly (February 1997, not 300% as stated — minor figure discrepancy but within same crisis period). Bread shortages confirmed. Broadly verified.

title: Mass Protests Storm Parliament â€” BSP Government Falls
reason: January 1997 storming of National Assembly; BSP resigned; Ivan Kostov center-right government followed. Confirmed.

title: Currency Board Introduced â€” Lev Pegged to Deutsche Mark
reason: July 1, 1997; 1000:1 peg to Deutsche Mark; hyperinflation halted immediately. Re-pegged to euro January 4, 1999. Confirmed.

title: Bulgarian Nurses Arrested in Libya on Fabricated HIV Charges
reason: Year is wrong. Nurses were arrested February/March 1999, not 1998. The HIV infections allegedly occurred in 1998 but arrests were in 1999. Year-off by 1 = FALSE.

title: EU Accession Negotiations Formally Opened
reason: EU formally opened accession negotiations with Bulgaria in 1999. Confirmed.

title: Former Tsar Simeon II Wins Elections and Becomes Prime Minister
reason: NDSV swept June 2001 elections; Simeon Saxe-Coburg-Gotha became PM — first former monarch to return to executive power via democratic election. Confirmed.

title: Bulgaria Joins NATO
reason: March 29, 2004 NATO accession confirmed.

reason: Signed April 25, 2005 in Luxembourg; January 1, 2007 accession date. Confirmed.

reason: January 1, 2007 EU accession alongside Romania. Confirmed.

title: EU Cooperation and Verification Mechanism Imposed on Bulgaria

reason: GERB won 2009 elections with ~40% of vote; Borisov former police chief and Sofia mayor. Confirmed.

reason: January 2009 gas cutoff through Ukraine affected Bulgaria for ~two weeks. Energy dependency and security debate confirmed.

reason: July 18, 2012; five Israeli tourists + one Bulgarian bus driver killed (six total); Hezbollah implicated; led to EU terrorist designation of Hezbollah military wing in 2013. Confirmed.

title: Mass Anti-Corruption Protests Topple Two Governments
reason: Borisov resigned February 2013 over electricity/corruption; Oresharski cabinet faced months of daily protests starting June 2013 and resigned 2014. Confirmed.

reason: Radev (BSP-backed, former Air Force Commander) won November 2016 presidential election; Borisov resigned immediately after defeat. Confirmed.

reason: July 2020 protests lasting 100+ days; gold bars/cash image trigger; targeted government-oligarch-prosecutor connections. Confirmed.

reason: July 10, 2020 ERM II accession; lev locked to euro at 1.95583. Confirmed.

reason: First cases March 2020; Bulgaria had lowest EU vaccination rate throughout pandemic; high mortality compounding demographic crisis. Confirmed.

reason: Three elections: April 4, July 11, November 14, 2021. ITN (entertainer's party) and PP (technocratic) rose; GERB/BSP lost dominance. Confirmed.
